newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander says to unify investment units.
newsitem.headline: Santander says to unify investment units.

text.p: Spain's Banco Santander said on Monday it was to unify its group treasury, asset management and corporate banking activities, achieving savings of four billion pesetas in the first year.
Up to now, these activities had been managed separately between Banco Santander and the investment banking arm Santander Investment.
In a statement, the bank said the move was in the light of Spain's likely membership of European Economic and Monetary Union and aimed at preparing the group for the new challenges involved.

Executive vice-president Ana Patricia Botin will be responsible for treasury, mutual and pension fund management and insurance, while Executive vice-president Juan Rodriguez Inciarte will be responsible for market and credit risk at home and abroad.
The department of organisation and cost control will be headed by Jose Ramon Jimenez, joining the bank as senior vice-president and responsible for implementing greater operating efficiency.
